description: An admin changes the background-job concurrency setting in the web UI. The request is handled by one server process but jobs run in a different one. Explain how the job-running process learns about the change and applies it.
anchor_note: non-bug task: root_cause_symbols holds the anchor (entry point / changed symbol); RC metrics are reported for category A only

source.verification: server/src/services/queue.service.spec.ts describe 'onConfigUpdate' test 'should update concurrency' (lines 22-23) covers only the last hops. The relay (serverSend/afterInit) has no test found - UNVERIFIED. The claim that no code other than NotificationService.onConfigUpdate sends ConfigUpdate was checked by grep of serverSend in server/src (only hls/transcoding and maintenance otherwise).
source.notes: Two processes in one docker container share Redis; the relay is implicit (nothing in SystemConfigService mentions it). Note an earlier draft in immich-analysis.md named app.repository.ts as the adapter site; that was wrong, the adapter is middleware/websocket.adapter.ts (corrected).

evidence: server/src/repositories/websocket.repository.ts:19-31 serverEvents list includes ConfigUpdate; :80-84 re-emit; :117-120 serverSend
server/src/middleware/websocket.adapter.ts:21-24 createAdapter(pubClient, subClient); installed at server/src/app.common.ts:64 and server/src/workers/microservices.ts:27
server/src/repositories/event.repository.ts:235-245 skips non-server handlers for server events

notes: Path verified: updateAdminConfig emits ConfigUpdate (system-config.service.ts:101) -> NotificationService.onConfigUpdate -> websocketRepository.serverSend (notification.service.ts:111-115) -> redis socket.io adapter (websocket.adapter.ts:13-25) -> afterInit server.on handler -> EventRepository.onEvent (websocket.repository.ts:79-86) -> QueueService.onConfigUpdate (server:true, Microservices branch, queue.service.ts:66-71) -> updateConcurrency -> JobRepository.setConcurrency (job.repository.ts:147-155).

Missing important step: the microservices process creates its own socket.io server with the Redis adapter (src/workers/microservices.ts:12-30, app.listen(0)); without it the receive side does not exist.
SystemConfigService.onConfigUpdate (system-config.service.ts:70-74) is also a server:true listener (clears config cache in every process) - borderline relevant, should not be an explicit distractor.
